question: The radius of a nucleus is given by $R = R_{0}A^{1/3}$. Calculate the radius of a nucleus with mass number $A = 216$, taking $R_{0} = 1.2 \times 10^{-15}\,\text{m}$. Also compare its radius with a nucleus having $A = 27$.

options.A:
For $A=216$, $R=1.2\times10^{-15}\times216^{1/3}=1.2\times10^{-15}\times6=7.2\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{m}$.
Compared with $A=27$, $\dfrac{R_{216}}{R_{27}}=(216/27)^{1/3}=2$, so the $A=216$ nucleus has twice the radius.
options.B: For $A=216$, $R=1.2\times10^{-15}\times216=2.592\times10^{-13}\,\mathrm{m}$. It has eight times the radius of the $A=27$ nucleus.
options.C: For $A=216$, $R=1.2\times10^{-15}/6=2.0\times10^{-16}\,\mathrm{m}$. It has half the radius of the $A=27$ nucleus.
options.D: For $A=216$, $R=6.0\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{m}$. Both nuclei have the same radius.
